name: Haven
basis: Vanta's own world of Havenbrooke: modern fantasy in the real autumn of 2009, with supernatural peoples recognized under federal law since 1867. The town, the university and their people are written for Prospero's Dungeon.
summary: A Finger Lakes mill town of about 35,000 on the Haven River, and Havenbrooke University on the east bank, where five thousand students of every people study over three ley lines. Autumn 2009: recession outside the gates, flip phones inside them.

intensity.voice: intimate, wry and adult: a campus drama where comedy and hurt share a page, every institution claims someone, and sex is written as part of who people are

curated-2026-10.title: Haven written for Prospero's Dungeon from Vanta's Havenbrooke material
curated-2026-10.license: Vanta's own setting; all rights reserved
curated-2026-10.note: Drawn from the Havenbrooke world and university documents. Prices are typical for upstate New York in 2009. Every business and person named is fictional.

neighborhoods.name: Havenbrooke campus
neighborhoods.summary: The university on the east bank: teaching halls round the Quad, Lantern Way running from the gates to Morrowe Commons, the dorms on the ridge and Ironroot Woods to the west. Three ley lines meet under it.

neighborhoods.name: Greek Row
neighborhoods.summary: The north edge of campus and the lane off Lantern Way where the fraternity and sorority houses stand, each with its own wards, rules and history.

neighborhoods.name: Downtown Haven
neighborhoods.summary: The west bank: Main Street, Chapel Street and the central plaza, brick storefronts from the 1880s, the pub, the diner, the bookshop and the cafe everyone uses as an office.

neighborhoods.name: the Mill District
neighborhoods.summary: The old paper mills south along the river: studios, galleries, loading docks turned into patios, a tattoo shop and the club in the unmarked warehouse.

neighborhoods.name: West Haven
neighborhoods.summary: Run-down Victorians and Craftsman houses on Elm, Birch and Sycamore, rented to students in groups of four to eight. Cheap, loud, and the plumbing is a rumor.

neighborhoods.name: Chapel Hill
neighborhoods.summary: Historic houses climbing the east side between downtown and campus, where faculty live behind porches and good hedges.

neighborhoods.name: Crane Ridge
neighborhoods.summary: The wooded northern ridge above West Haven, most of it behind the Crane family's fence. The road up has one gas station and a tavern that closes early.

places.name: Aldwright Hall
places.summary: Esoteric Sciences in the oldest building on campus: dark brick, cold stone floors, chalk dust and the smell of misfired spells. The third-floor windows never latch.

places.name: Vespers Hall
places.summary: The ritual complex over the strongest ley node: candlelit chambers and spell rings cut into black stone that warms underfoot. Booked weeks ahead.

places.name: the Old Observatory
places.summary: A stone tower from the founding with an open roof and locked lower floors. People go up to breathe.

places.name: Kaelen Hall
places.summary: Interpersonal Dynamics in a converted 1920s sanatorium: a tall atrium, couches in every hallway, lavender and beeswax, and an ethics room that looks out on the cemetery.

places.name: Warden Hall
places.summary: Military and Tactical Operations: squat concrete, gun oil from the armory, cameras in the training rooms and classes at seven in the morning.

places.name: Thornewall
places.summary: Mundane Studies in nineties glass and industrial carpet, under a suppression field that hums. Witches get headaches; humans finally relax.
spots: the Oracle office in the basement

places.name: the Mirren Media Studio
places.summary: The communications studio: a small TV set, two edit bays and the WHAV-FM booth, with a sign that says ON AIR in red.

places.name: Bellweather Hall
places.summary: Supernatural Physiology and Integration: red-brick Georgian with a modern wing, anatomy labs upstairs and a faint smell of preservative.

places.name: Farrow House
places.summary: The supervised treatment house: a Victorian with a wraparound porch, walls that swallow sound and a stained-glass owl over the waiting room door.

places.name: Chancellor Wynne Library
places.summary: The main library, whose shelves rearrange overnight to the course schedule. The basement archives need a sponsor and a blood signature.

places.name: the Verdant Grove
places.summary: Four linked ritual greenhouses, warm and humid all year, and an outdoor garden for plants too charged to keep inside. The Enchanters' Guild workshop is at the back.

places.name: Stitch Hall Ateliers
places.summary: Fashion studios: fabric to the ceiling, rows of industrial machines and long mirrors, private ateliers upstairs.

places.name: Evermere Health Pavilion
places.summary: Six floors of human and supernatural medicine that never close: lycan rooms, fae springs in the sub-basement and consent-warded feeding suites.

places.name: Crestfall Arena
places.summary: The athletic complex, reinforced for lycan sparring and aerial fae training. The auxiliary studio is empty at four in the morning.

places.name: Morrowe Commons
places.summary: Four floors of lounges, food counters, music rooms and club space under a ward that keeps aura pressure off humans. The bakery opens at six.

places.name: the Commons coffee bar
places.summary: The coffee counter on the ground floor of Morrowe, with a line at 7:55 and tables nobody gives up after 9.

places.name: Caldwell Fountain Court
places.summary: A plaza round a fountain three degrees colder than the air, with a faint pull that draws confessions out of tired people.

places.name: Ridgewalk Chapel
places.summary: A small white clapboard chapel at the western edge of campus: twelve pews, always unlocked, one candle that someone keeps lit.

places.name: the Quad and Lantern Way
places.summary: Four acres of green under old oaks, and the gas-lamp path from the gates to Morrowe that everyone calls the runway.

places.name: Ironroot Woods
places.summary: A mile of old-growth forest on the west edge of campus. The trails are kept by day; after dusk the lycans run and the witches gather.

places.name: the back woods
places.summary: Off the kept trails, in the woods and hills that run west and south of Haven: second-growth forest, old stone walls, hunting stands and no signal.
spots: a stone wall in the trees
a rise with a view of the lake

places.name: the Old Cemetery
places.summary: Granite stones behind an overgrown iron fence, older than the university, where some headstones are not where they were last week.

places.name: Nexus Housing
places.summary: Upperclass suites with kitchens over a secondary ley node: magic works better, sleep is worse. The third floor is three units round a shared common room.

places.name: North Dorm Ridge
places.summary: Three brutalist towers with reinforced doors and air tuned for demon heat and vampire chill. Humans are told to take the stairs.

places.name: the East Residential Quad
places.summary: Three brick dorms round a courtyard used for spell tests, frisbee and breakups, in that order through the day.

places.name: Alpha Gamma House
places.summary: A gray three-story Victorian with black trim, a basement nobody outside the pack sees on a full moon, and couches that make human guests feel strange.

places.name: Sigma Theta Hex House
places.summary: An ivy-covered federal mansion with black shutters, sage and iron in the air, and everything above the grand staircase for sisters only.

places.name: Phi Sigma Nox House
places.summary: The vampire-led house: a brick Georgian with heavy curtains, a wine cellar and parties that start after the dining halls close.

places.name: Omicron Phi Ember House
places.summary: The demonkin house: warm, loud, scented, and very careful about who it lets upstairs.

places.name: the Row snack bar
places.summary: A sandwich window at the end of Greek Row that stays open until two on weekends and sells more coffee than food.

places.name: the Stag & Thistle
places.summary: The pub on a Main Street corner: forty taps, scotch eggs and shepherd's pie, faculty in the back booths and students in the front. The owner has never been wrong about an ID.

places.name: Midnight Gas
places.summary: The 24-hour diner on North Main: neon, cracked vinyl booths, stewed coffee and pancakes at three in the morning.

places.name: Pale Press Coffee
places.summary: A cafe in an old print shop on Prescott Alley: brick, big windows and espresso. No glamours, no charms, no spellwork, by house rule.
spots: the back room with the old press

places.name: Drothe's Bookery
places.summary: A two-story used bookshop on Bell Street: five-dollar paperbacks downstairs, occult texts upstairs at whatever price Drothe names.

places.name: Harper's
places.summary: The good restaurant at Main and Chapel: white cloths, hurricane candles, a long wine list and the best bread in the Finger Lakes.

places.name: the Haven Saturday Market
places.summary: The farmers market in the central plaza, moved into the old meeting hall for winter: produce, cheese, honey and dryad-made preserves.

places.name: Bianchi's Pizza
places.summary: A slice counter on Main with a two-slices-and-a-soda special and a jukebox that only takes quarters.

places.name: the Strand
places.summary: A single-screen 1920s movie house showing one new release and a midnight cult film on Fridays.

places.name: the Main Street bus shelter
places.summary: Where the Haven Transit buses and the twice-daily shuttle to Ithaca stop, opposite the bank clock.

places.name: Kessel Drugs
places.summary: The pharmacy and general store on Chapel Street: prescriptions, cold medicine, condoms, phone cards and a photo counter.

places.name: the Velvet Spire
places.summary: The supernatural-friendly club in an unmarked three-story warehouse: DJs below, private booths in the middle, and a members-only top floor.
spots: the stairs to the top floor

places.name: Arrow & Ink
places.summary: A tattoo and piercing shop on Foundry Lane, lamp-lit, with enchanted ink for clients the owner trusts.

places.name: the Ironworks Collective
places.summary: Eighteen artisan studios on Old Foundry Row, renting bench space with charm infusion included.

places.name: the Foundry Taproom
places.summary: A brewpub in an old loading dock with a patio over the river and a band most Thursdays.

places.name: the Elm Street houses
places.summary: Student rentals on Elm with sagging porches, red cups on the lawn and the party everyone talks about the next morning.

places.name: Birch Street
places.summary: Where Delta Nu Iris and Delta Omicron Theta keep their houses, a block apart and not speaking.

places.name: Sal's Corner Deli
places.summary: A corner store and deli on Sycamore with hero sandwiches, cheap beer and a cashier who has seen everything.

places.name: the Sycamore Laundromat
places.summary: Coin washers, a broken change machine and the best place in Haven to overhear a breakup.

places.name: Linden Street Bakery
places.summary: A faculty-heavy bakery with scones, quiet tables and a bulletin board of house-sitting jobs.

places.name: the Riverwalk
places.summary: Three miles of path along the east bank from downtown past the mills into the hills, with benches, lamps and small docks. Nobody clears the ice.
spots: the bench with the view of the ridge

places.name: Crane Hill
places.summary: The Crane family's fenced and gated estate on the ridge, home to a line of vampires since 1819. Visitors are expected or turned away.

places.name: the Ridge Road Tavern
places.summary: A low roadhouse at the foot of the ridge where the Cranes' staff drink and students do not, mostly.

transit.name: On foot
transit.summary: Campus is fifteen minutes end to end; downtown is a ten-minute walk over the footbridge.

transit.name: The Havenbrooke shuttle
transit.summary: A free loop from the gates to downtown every twenty minutes until midnight, and twice a day to Ithaca.

transit.name: Haven Transit
transit.summary: Two city bus lines, a dollar a ride, running until nine.

transit.name: A car
transit.summary: Most students do not have one, and the ones who do are very popular on Friday.

careers.name: Licensed enchanter
careers.summary: Making and selling charms that carry a DED compliance mark, from a stall, a studio or a dorm room.

careers.name: Campus security officer
careers.summary: Patrolling Havenbrooke under MTO-trained supervisors and writing up whatever the Dean's office will want in the morning.

careers.name: Ward technician
careers.summary: Testing, patching and certifying building wards for the university and the town.

careers.name: Dining hall worker
careers.summary: Line, dish pit and bakery shifts at Morrowe Commons, mostly students on work-study.

employers.name: Havenbrooke University
employers.summary: The university and the town's largest employer: faculty, clinics, dining, grounds and security.

employers.name: Evermere Health Pavilion
employers.summary: The campus hospital, open all hours.

employers.name: the Student Enchanters' Guild
employers.summary: The guild workshop at the Verdant Grove, which takes student commissions.

employers.name: the Crane estate
employers.summary: Groundskeepers, drivers and house staff for the family on the ridge, paid well and told little.

employers.name: the Oracle
employers.summary: The student paper, in the Thornewall basement.

career_hubs.name: The university
career_hubs.summary: Most paychecks in Haven come from Havenbrooke, one way or another.

career_hubs.name: Main Street and the mills
career_hubs.summary: Bars, cafes, shops and studios, mostly staffed by students.

climate.summary: Upstate New York: long gray winters with lake-effect snow, a muddy spring, warm wet summers and a short bright fall.

months.note: Lake-effect snow and a gray sky for weeks.
The coldest stretch; the Riverwalk is ice.
Mud and slush; spring term drags.
Warm and wet; the lakes fill with summer people.
The warmest month, thunderstorms most afternoons.
Move-in heat at the end of the month.
Clear and cool; the term settles in.
Peak color in the first two weeks, then wind and rain.
Snow on the ground for finals.

annual_events.name: Move-in week
annual_events.summary: Parents, minivans and housing letters; the dorms fill and the wards get their annual check.

annual_events.name: The autumn equinox rites
annual_events.summary: The covens book every chamber in Vespers Hall; Sigma Theta Hex holds its rite in the largest.

annual_events.name: The Harvest Howl
annual_events.summary: Alpha Gamma's Halloween bonfire on the north practice fields, the biggest party of the fall.

annual_events.name: The winter charm exhibit
annual_events.summary: The Enchanters' Guild shows the term's work at the Verdant Grove the week before finals.

annual_events.name: The Creative Collective spring show
annual_events.summary: Student art, fashion and music in the Ironworks studios over one weekend.

annual_events.name: The NSAC sparring bracket
annual_events.summary: Intercollegiate supernatural sparring at Crestfall Arena; the Crows have not won since 1998.

local_color.name: The runway
local_color.summary: Lantern Way, because everyone sees everyone on it sooner or later.

local_color.name: Fountain confessions
local_color.summary: Most breakups and hookups on campus are said to start at Caldwell Fountain, which pulls the truth out of tired people.

local_color.name: The moving headstones
local_color.summary: Some stones in the Old Cemetery are a few feet from where they were last week, and a physics major once measured it.

local_color.name: Nexus dreams
local_color.summary: Everyone in Nexus Housing dreams harder and sleeps worse, and the housing office does not put that in the brochure.

local_color.name: Three a.m. pancakes
local_color.summary: A short stack and stewed coffee at Midnight Gas after anything at all.

local_color.name: The Crestfall Crows
local_color.summary: The university teams, loved loudly and expected to lose.

local_color.name: "Mundie"
local_color.summary: What some supernatural students call a non-magical human. Said to their face, it starts fights.

local_color.name: The chapel candle
local_color.summary: The candle in Ridgewalk Chapel has been burning since before anyone on staff was hired, and nobody has ever seen it lit.

prices.item: Amtrak from Syracuse to New York

notables.name: Delia Okonkwo
notables.about: A witch from an old Boston lineage who opened Pale Press so nobody would have to perform in it. She asks you to leave once, politely.
notables.wants: to keep one room in Haven where nobody uses anything on anybody

notables.name: Betsari Kavanagh
notables.about: An Appalachian-trained witch who tattoos by day and does enchanted ink for people she trusts. Funny, blunt and impossible to rush.
notables.wants: one client this month who actually knows what they are asking for

notables.name: Drothe
notables.about: The keeper of the bookshop on Bell Street, a witch nobody can classify. Prices change with their mood and with who is asking.
notables.wants: to see which students come upstairs this term, and for what

notables.name: Gideon Vale
notables.about: A mundane human who has run the Crane household for thirty years and is the only person Haven PD speaks to about the ridge.
notables.wants: to keep the family out of the papers through one more election

notables.name: Mireille Thorne-Ashford
notables.about: Senior incantation faculty and advisor to Sigma Theta Hex. Exacting, unhurried, and more interested in why a working failed than in the student who failed it.
notables.wants: one student this year who can hold a working under real pressure

notables.name: Kasper Innes
notables.about: Teaches IPD 340, the consent course every SPI and ES student has to pass. Gentle in the lecture hall and merciless in office hours.
notables.wants: to make someone in the back row say what they actually think

notables.name: Marcus Halbrook
notables.about: A retired colonel, bitten in the line of duty, who runs MTO like a unit and starts every class at seven sharp.
notables.wants: a cohort that passes the federal review without anyone getting hurt

notables.name: Iolana Whitestone
notables.about: A retired succubus diplomat who teaches SPI 220 and runs the clinical placements at Farrow House.
notables.wants: her students to stop being embarrassed by the word hunger

notables.name: Samuel Park
notables.about: Heads computer science, runs the Ashforth lab and has opinions about everyone's variable names.
notables.wants: a student who can make the lab servers stop crashing during the full moon

notables.name: Imogen Shaw
notables.about: Teaches media and communications, ran a newsroom for fifteen years and still edits everything in red pen.
notables.wants: one honest story out of her seminar this term
